title_key: orchestrate an ai secure martech simulation for systems thinking and industry ready capability|lekakis
title: Orchestrate: An AI-secure MarTech simulation for systems thinking and industry-ready capability
abstract:
Marketing technology (MarTech) education has traditionally emphasised the acquisition of discrete platform skills, often resulting in fragmented, “tool-first” approaches that inadequately prepare graduates to manage complex MarTech ecosystems. At the same time, the rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has intensified concerns about whether conventional assessment designs can validly evaluate higher-order capabilities such as judgement, strategic reasoning, and decision making (Corbin et al., 2025; Zeng et al., 2024). These converging challenges highlight an urgent need for Technology Enhanced Learning (TEL) innovations grounded in human-centred design that foster systems thinking and strategic decision making while providing authentic, AI-resilient assessment opportunities.
This presentation introduces Orchestrate, a low-fidelity (LoFi) MarTech simulation designed to cultivate systems thinking and assess industry-ready capability development in undergraduate and postgraduate marketing programs. Developed in Microsoft Excel, a widely available and low-barrier technology, the simulation provides a scalable and accessible learning experience. Informed by industry practice, Orchestrate positions students as marketing leaders responsible for managing investments across an interconnected MarTech ecosystem. Piloted during Semester 1, 2026, with Bachelor of Commerce students undertaking the Marketing Technology major at RMIT University, student teams balanced competing priorities to optimise customer acquisition, retention, satisfaction, and revenue growth. Rather than learning isolated technologies, students allocated finite budgets across 12 capability areas aligned to the People, Process, Data, and Technology (PPDT) framework (Monshizada et al., 2023).
The pedagogical design is underpinned by systems thinking theory, which emphasises understanding interdependencies, trade-offs, and emergent patterns within complex systems (York et al., 2019). The simulation makes relationships between MarTech capabilities explicit, demonstrating that sustainable organisational performance emerges from balancing people, process, data, and technological priorities rather than investing in individual tools. Authentic assessment principles further situate learning within realistic professional contexts that mirror contemporary marketing practice.
A distinctive contribution of Orchestrate lies in its AI-resilient assessment design. Rather than relying on static written outputs that can readily be generated or enhanced by GenAI, assessment focuses on students’ situated decision making within the dynamic simulation environment. Teams must justify their evolving strategies, explain the consequences of their choices, and demonstrate alignment between investment decisions, course principles, and organisational performance outcomes. Because gameplay produces different conditions and outcomes for each team, the design reduces opportunities for inappropriate AI assistance while maintaining a focus on higher-order judgement and strategic reasoning. 
Early evidence from the Semester 1, 2026 pilot indicates strong student engagement and learning. Assessment submissions demonstrated sustained engagement with the simulation, while reflective responses showed strong understanding of course concepts and application of relevant theoretical frameworks to strategic decisions. Qualitative student experience survey feedback also identified Orchestrate as a key highlight of the course. These findings are indicative rather than the result of a formal research evaluation; a comprehensive Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) study is now being developed, with an ethics application underway, to investigate the simulation’s impact on systems thinking, strategic decision making, student engagement, and learning outcomes.

title_key: perceived forensic auditing learning digital forensic mindset and accounting students self reported cyber fraud readiness|syam
title: Perceived Forensic Auditing Learning, Digital Forensic Mindset, and Accounting Students' Self-Reported Cyber-Fraud Readiness
abstract:
Purpose: This study examines how perceived forensic auditing learning and a digital forensic mindset are associated, individually and jointly, with accounting students’ self-reported readiness to address cyber fraud in the generative AI era.
Research Method: A quantitative survey involved 34 accounting students who had completed a Forensic Auditing course. Fifteen five-point Likert items measured the three constructs, and the responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics, item–total correlations, Cronbach’s alpha, and multiple linear regression.
Results and Discussion: Both predictors had positive, statistically significant conditional associations with perceived readiness. The joint regression model was statistically significant, and the standardized coefficient for digital forensic mindset was numerically larger.
Implications: Accounting curricula may benefit from linking forensic auditing concepts to critical evaluation of electronic evidence and cyber-risk scenarios.
Originality: The study examines subject-specific forensic auditing learning alongside an investigative digital mindset in explaining variation in accounting students’ perceived cyber-fraud readiness.
authors: ["Hasnidar Syam", "A. N. Y. Amran", "Nur Aliyah", "Amelia Dwi Cahya Wardani"]

title_key: designing authentic learning through anchor scenarios a whole of unit approach|alksnis
title: Designing authentic learning through anchor scenarios: A whole-of-unit approach
abstract:
In technology disciplines, students are more engaged and better prepared for employment when they experience technical work as purposeful professional practice rather than as isolated exercises (Kerven et al., 2017). Generative AI can now produce working code, configured systems and polished documentation, so students can complete tasks that mainly ask for these outputs without doing much of the work themselves. Such tasks are unlikely to hold students’ interest, and the work submitted can be weak evidence of capability. The professional judgement remains theirs: deciding what should be built, for whom, within which constraints, and with what consequences. The challenge for curriculum design is to integrate, teach and assess that judgement.
This presentation describes a curriculum design we developed in response. Each unit is set in one authentic workplace context, the anchor scenario, which defines the stakeholders, constraints and outcome for the whole unit. Every session then presents a session scenario: a professional decision in that context, building on the one before. In the final assessment, students deliver the outcome the anchor scenario set. Content is taught when students need it for a decision, and assessment is set in the same context.
The approach draws on situated learning, in which judgement develops through authentic activity in realistic contexts (Brown et al., 1989; Lave & Wenger, 1991), and on Action Mapping, which begins from a real workplace outcome and derives the decisions learners must make before selecting content (Moore, 2017). Narrative carries more force when scenarios accumulate rather than stand alone (Bruner, 1991). Sustained scenario structures have precedents: anchored instruction centres on one extended problem (Cognition and Technology Group at Vanderbilt, 1990), media computation organises content coverage (Guzdial, 2003), and task-driven case studies guide practice rather than judgement (Porubän et al., 2024). None spans an entire unit while structuring cumulative professional decisions, producing employer-facing artefacts, and giving AI a purposeful role.
Each unit is built in three phases. The Anchor phase derives the scenario from a workplace outcome and produces a unit design plan mapping outcomes to assessments and giving every session its own scenario. The Embed phase scripts each session in full, writing assessments at the same time and checking alignment in both directions (Biggs, 1996), with every activity carrying a short connection back to the scenario. The Shift phase builds the design as web-based learning paths for delivery on campus, online or in hybrid mode.
This approach now runs in more than 30 units across five discipline areas. They include a café point-of-sale system built over 11 programming sessions, a hospital network designed for a computer networking unit, and a robotic warehouse floor for an electrical engineering unit. The presentation walks through the designs themselves, alongside feedback from the teaching staff who delivered them. While the scenarios are varied, each design begins with the professional world and its people, derives the decisions from them, and lets the technology find its place inside that world.

title_key: a systematic review of how genai supports l2 oral proficiency development from the lens of self determination theory sdt|lin
title: A systematic review of how GenAI supports L2 oral proficiency development from the lens of Self-determination Theory (SDT)
abstract: Despite a proliferation of research on GenAI for second/foreign language (L2) education since the official launch of ChatGPT in November 2022, current understanding of its role in L2 oral proficiency development remains limited. To address this research gap, this systematic review draws on Self-Determination Theory (SDT) to examine how GenAI may support L2 learners’ three basic psychological needs and how such need satisfaction may be associated with their cognitive, behavioural, and emotional engagement in GenAI-mediated speaking. Adopting the PRISMA Statement (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses) approach, the review identified 30 empirical studies from ProQuest, Web of Science, and Scopus based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The selected studies were analysed using a hybrid deductive and inductive coding approach following a coding framework. The analysis suggests that GenAI can enhance L2 learners’ sense of autonomy satisfaction by enabling learner-driven choices and interaction personalisation. It may also support competence satisfaction by affording accessible oral practice, immediate and personalised feedback, and scaffolded speaking development. Regarding relatedness satisfaction, GenAI appears to offer partial support by providing a non-judgemental and emotionally supportive practice environment. Furthermore, the degree of needs satisfaction may be associated with learners’ behavioural, cognitive, and emotional engagement (or disengagement) in GenAI-supported L2 speaking development. Specifically, the findings suggest that emotional engagement in GenAI-mediated speaking appears most evident, followed by cognitive and behavioural engagement. These findings extend the SDT literature in GenAI-assisted language learning and offer practical insights for integrating emerging technologies into language education. For educators, given the review highlights the promising affordances of GenAI to address conventional barriers to L2 oral proficiency development, teachers should integrate GenAI into speaking classes to create an anxiety-free and feedback-rich speaking practice environment, while they need to consider learners’ age and proficiency to provide necessary teacher guidance.

title_key: blending seamless and seamful tactics to nurture practical and reflexive ai competences in design education|lupetti
title: Blending seamless and seamful tactics to nurture practical and reflexive AI competences in design education
abstract: The rapid integration of generative AI into design education generates tensions between innovation and pedagogy. This paper presents a pilot program that combines structured spaces for practical learning and critical reflection on generative AI. Implemented within a large undergraduate Storytelling and Animation course, the program combined seamless AI-based creative exercises with a deliberately seamful activity intended to disrupt automation and foreground human agency. By analysing student reflections collected through written reports, we find that this pedagogical program can foster diverse critical positionings, enabling students to negotiate authorship, question tool dependencies, and reappropriate creative processes. Rather than adopting or rejecting generative AI uncritically, students developed nuanced understandings of its role in their design practices. The main contribution of this work is to foreground the combination of seamless and seamful activities as a pedagogical tactic for teaching practical competences while encouraging critical reflexivity about the integration of generative AI into higher education.
venue: Proceedings of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Educator's Forum

title_key: towards a pedagogy for deliberate ai assisted programming in computer science education|amouroux
title: Towards a pedagogy for deliberate AI-assisted programming in computer science education
abstract: Generative AI is reshaping both higher education and professional software development, raising new challenges for how first-year computing students learn to program meaningfully. Recent research suggests novice programmers often engage with AI-assisted tools in ways that privilege speed and surface functionality over understanding, producing shallow prompting, limited code engagement, and reduced visibility of student reasoning. This paper proposes a five-stage pedagogical framework for deliberate AI-assisted programming in first-year computing, derived from the research team’s teaching practice, empirical studies of novice AI-assisted programming, and established software engineering practice. In doing so it reframes AI-assisted programming as a pedagogical design problem rather than a question of tool adoption or restriction, and offers a transferable model that preserves student responsibility for reasoning, validation, and understanding. As the first cycle of a design-based research study, the paper’s contribution is the framework and a mixed-methods evaluation plan through which it will be enacted and assessed in two first-year cohorts, rather than empirical findings.

title_key: effects of chatgpt assisted learning on students mathematical reasoning problem solving skills and achievement in bagmati provience of nepal|dhakal
title:
Effects of ChatGpt - Assisted Learning on Students’
Mathematical Reasoning, Problem- Solving skills and
Achievement in Bagmati Provience of Nepal
abstract:
The rapid development of artificial intellengence (AI) has created new opportunities
for improving mathematics teaching and learning. chatGPT, as a generative AI-based
conversational learning tool, can provide students with immediate feedback,
explanations, examples and alternative solution strategies. This study examines the
effects of ChatGPT- assisted learning on student’s mathematical reasoning, problem
solving ability and mathematical achievement in Bagmati Provience, Nepal. A quasi
experimental pre- test- post- test control group design was proposed for the study. The
study used the sample of 300 secondary- level students, comprising 150 in students
in the experimental group and 150 in the control group. The experimental group
received mathematics instruction supported by chatGPT, whereas the control group
received conventional instruction. Mathematical reasoning, problem solving and
achievement were measured through structured tests administered before and after
the intervention. The stimulated findings indicated that the experimental group
demonstrated greater improvement in all three outcomes. Mathematical reasoning
increased from a pre –test mean 24.80 to 36.70 , problem solving performance from
23.90 to 35.90 and mathematical achievement from 52.10 to 70.80. the corresponding
post- test mean for the contro group were 28.90, 28.40 and 61.50 respectively.
Independent- sample t- tests indicated statistically significant differences between
the groups for mathematical reasoning, t(197) = 16.02, P < 0.001, problem solving,
t(198) = 15.15, p < o.oo1 and achievement, t(196) = 16.51, P < o.oo1. The findings
suggest that chatGPT- assisted learning has potential as a supplementry approach
for enhancing mathematics learning. However, effective teacher guidance verification
of AI generated responses and responsible use of ChatGPT are essential to avoid
overdependence on AI. The study provides a basis for further empirical investigation
of generative AI supported mathematics education in Nepal.

title_key: evaluating generative ai in chemistry prelabs efficiency gains without measurable learning benefits|fernandez
title:
Evaluating Generative AI in Chemistry Prelabs: Efficiency
Gains without Measurable Learning Benefits
abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools in higher education has raised questions regarding their impact on students’ information literacy (IL) and cognitive processes. In this study, we investigated how generative AI influences undergraduate students’ performance and perceptions in an inorganic chemistry prelaboratory assignment consisting in gathering and elaborating information relevant to the experiments. Second-year chemistry students completed two prelab tasks: one with generative AI support and one without AI. Students reported that generative AI support significantly reduced time dedicated to prelab elaboration. They also perceived AI-assisted tasks as easier and faster, rated AI-generated information as less clear and precise than traditional sources, and frequently expressed concerns about its reliability. However, no statistically significant differences were observed in instructor-evaluated scores between AI-supported and non-AI prelabs. These results indicate that students predominantly valued AI for efficiency. Interpreted through a Cognitive Load Theory lens, the reduction in time and search effort is consistent with a possible decrease in task-related logistical demands.
authors: ["Alberto A. Fern\u00e1ndez", "M. L\u00f3pez-Torres", "Jes\u00fas J. Fern\u00e1ndez", "Digna V\u00e1zquez-Garc\u00eda"]

title_key: optimalisasi pemanfaatan artificial intelligence dalam pengembangan perangkat pembelajaran inovatif bagi guru sma|amelia
title: Optimalisasi Pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence dalam Pengembangan Perangkat Pembelajaran Inovatif bagi Guru SMA
abstract: Digital transformation in education requires teachers to be competent in utilizing technology specifically Artificial Intelligence (AI) to develop innovative learning materials tailored to students' needs. This community service initiative aimed to enhance the knowledge, skills, and competencies of high school teachers in optimizing AI for the development of innovative learning resources. The program was conducted on May 23, 2026, at SMA Negeri 2 Painan, comprising several stages: initial observation, training, technology implementation, mentoring and evaluation, and sustainability planning. The training introduced various AI platforms such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Teachy AI, and PhetColorado to support the preparation of course materials, the development of learning media, and the design of more interactive learning activities. Based on the results from 50 participants who completed the questionnaire and submitted their work, 76% of the participating teachers have achieved competency in using AI to support the development of instructional materials. Furthermore, the training encouraged some participants to transition from merely being familiar with the technology to actively applying it in their professional practice. These findings suggest that training combined with hands-on practice and mentoring has the potential to strengthen teachers' digital capacity. Nevertheless, the use of AI must be accompanied by the ability to verify information, uphold academic integrity, and adapt AI-generated outputs to the specific characteristics of the students. Consequently, this community service initiative contributes to strengthening teachers' digital competencies and supports a transformation toward learning that is innovative, adaptive, and sustainable.
authors: ["Puspa Amelia", "K. Khairudin", "F. Zuzano", "S. Herawati", "Niniwati Niniwati", "Yusri Wahyuni", "R. Desfitri", "Fauziah Fauziah"]

title_key: research on ai empowered pedagogical reform in programming education|ge
title: Research on AI-Empowered Pedagogical Reform in Programming Education
abstract: The swift spread of generative artificial intelligence has thoroughly transformed the educational mindset and practical modes of programming instruction. Modern AI platforms are capable of autonomously producing source code, troubleshooting glitches, and refining software scripts, creating unparalleled obstacles for conventional teaching systems that prioritize syntax tutoring and coding competency cultivation. The present paper first conducts a thorough review and analysis of 40 empirical studies, and further consolidates hands-on reform practices sourced from numerous colleges and universities. It comprehensively investigates the current development status, common dilemmas, and targeted solutions for embedding AI technologies within programming teaching. This research indicates that the efficient application of artificial intelligence tools within coding classes is closely associated with elaborately designed teaching tactics, optimized evaluation systems, and phased incorporation schemes. Excessive reliance on AI is likely to inhibit learners' advanced thinking capabilities; on the contrary, well-developed AI learning assistants with guided interactive functions can greatly boost academic performance. Drawing on the above analysis, the paper advances a three-party joint teaching system: artificial intelligence works as a thinking collaborator, educators function as instructional mentors, and undergraduates play the part of autonomous knowledge creators. Meanwhile, a three-stage execution blueprint is formulated, covering basic auxiliary backing, contrastive introspection, and cooperative innovation. Relying on real-world statistics obtained from 120 student respondents, the present paper explores the varied influences of AI aid on learners holding different learning bases. The conclusions deliver theoretical references and operational instructions for the smart reform of programming teaching.
venue: 2026 International Conference on Computer Science, Technology and Engineering (ICCSTE)

title_key: generative ai assisted development of browser based docking notebooks a chatgpt vibe coding methodology for chemistry and pharmacy education|sayed
title:
Generative-AI-Assisted
Development of Browser-Based
Docking Notebooks: A ChatGPT “Vibe Coding” Methodology
for Chemistry and Pharmacy Education
abstract: Molecular docking is widely taught in medicinal chemistry and pharmacy programs, yet student participation is frequently limited by software installation barriers, platform incompatibilities, and uneven access to computational resources. This report describes a generative-AI-assisted (“vibe coding”) methodology in which ChatGPT is used to iteratively draft, refine, and debug Google Colab notebooks that deliver an install-free docking experience through a web browser. Because Colab executes Python in the browser and requires no local setup, the workflow can be run on laptops or mobile devices, supporting equitable access for students. Two notebooks are reported: (i) single-ligand docking to a single receptor with SMILES input, pH-aware structure preparation, autodetection of a docking box from a co-crystallized ligand when present, and student-editable sampling parameters (grid, exhaustiveness, poses, verbosity, seed) and (ii) a library-screening notebook that accepts a SMILES list, prepares ligands in parallel with pH control, executes batch docking, and exports ranked results for analysis. The central educational contribution is not only the notebook itself but a reproducible prompt → code → test loop that enables instructors to construct browser-deployable computational notebooks, which students with minimal coding experience can then run and modify at the parameter level while practicing verification, scientific reasoning, and responsible AI disclosure.

title_key: experts avoiders and in betweens creating a quadrant model for the identification of different llm user groups within the student body|schelling
title: Experts, Avoiders, and In-Betweens: Creating a Quadrant Model for the Identification of Different LLM User Groups Within the Student Body
abstract: Since the release of ChatGPT, AI assistants based on Large Language Models (LLM) have quickly made their way into higher education. Whether this new generation of chatbots can be used to effectively drive learning processes, however, depends on an equally new digital skill: prompt engineering. Considering both educational commitments and legal restrictions, this article addresses the questions of why and how students in higher education, especially in the European Union, need to be introduced to prompt engineering if they are to successfully integrate LLM-based chatbots into their self-study processes. Against the backdrop of the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and existing research on the factors influencing university students’ AI use, this article presents a quadrant model meant to help educators and researchers assess the characteristic skills and needs of four different LLM user groups within the student body: the AI-confident Experts, the LLM-shy Avoiders, plus the Improvisers and Independents who fall somewhere in between these extremes. Focusing on students’ AI-related learning anxiety and learning self-efficacy as two factors that influence LLM adoption, we discuss how these four target groups might be best supported, both individually and as a heterogeneous student body.

title_key: from information delivery to cognitive co creation how generative ai enhances computational thinking education through student authored visualizations|zhou
title: From information delivery to cognitive co-creation: how generative AI enhances computational thinking education through student-authored visualizations
МЕТОДИЧНІ АСПЕКТИ ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЇ НАВЧАЛЬНИХ ЗАВДАНЬ З ІНФОРМАТИЧНИХ ДИСЦИПЛІН ДЛЯ СТУДЕНТІВ ЕКОНОМІЧНИХ СПЕЦІАЛЬНОСТЕЙ В ЕПОХУ ГЕНЕРАТИВНОГО ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ
abstract: The article analyzes the didactic crisis posed by the use of traditional educational tasks in computer science disciplines amid the rapid spread of artificial intelligence technologies. The active use of generative artificial intelligence tools in the professional activities of economists and in higher education necessitates the updating of classical pedagogical approaches. The aim of the article is to theoretically substantiate and develop methodological principles for adapting and transforming educational tasks in computer science disciplines for students of economic specialties. The research methodology is based on the integration of the AAAE framework, AIAS, P. Hardman's post-AI taxonomy of learning, and the concept of embedded validity. The feasibility of moving from traditional summative control to process-oriented assessment is substantiated, with the key subject of analysis being the student's immediate cognitive trajectory, rather than a ready-made computational or software product. The scientific novelty of the work lies in the systematization of the fundamental methodological principles of the transformation of educational tasks, as well as in the development of five levels of integration of AI tools in teaching computer science disciplines to students of economic specialties (from "Fundamental" to "Research") with a detailed description of the role of AI, the content of the student's activity and the focus of pedagogical assessment for each of them. A procedural model for performing AI-integrated tasks is systematically structured, comprising the following sequential steps: problem formulation, AI planning, independent execution, critical analysis of AI recommendations, and final professional reflection. The proposed approach transforms AI from a threat to academic integrity into a powerful learning tool, contributing to the development of critical thinking and professional analytical competencies of future economists.
venue: Сучасні інформаційні технології та інноваційні методики навчання в підготовці фахівців: методологія, теорія, досвід, проблеми

title_key: research on the cultivation of ai teaching competence for primary and secondary school teachers in the context of generative artificial intelligence|gao
title: Research on the Cultivation of AI Teaching Competence for Primary and Secondary School Teachers in the Context of Generative Artificial Intelligence
abstract: In the context of the global digital transformation of education, generative artificial intelligence has transformed the entire teaching process of primary and secondary schools, including lesson planning, classroom teaching, individualized teaching and learning assessment, and poses unprecedented challenges to teachers' professional competence. The AI teaching competence stems from the TPACK theory. It is teachers’ holistic ability to use generative AI tools for subject teaching, assess the quality of AI-generated products, prevent educational ethical risks, and carry out human AI collaborative teaching, which has become a key indicator of teachers' digital literacy in the AI era. Current research shows that most primary and secondary school teachers lack deep understanding of generative AI, misuse AI tools, and fail to effectively integrate AI with subject teaching, and insufficient awareness of data privacy and academic integrity risks. Localized cultivation strategies for Chinese primary and secondary school teachers are lacking. To address this gap, this paper selects mainland China' s inservice primary and secondary school teachers as its research subjects and uses mixed research methods such as questionnaire survey, semistructured interview and case study. In line with the four dimensional competency connotation suggested by Tripathi et al. (2025) , this paper adjusts the measurement scale for teachers' AI teaching competence and gathers valid data from 200 frontline teachers in order to fully explore the current status, differences among groups and barriers of teachers' AI teaching competence. The research reveals that the overall AI teaching competence of primary and secondary school teachers is at mediumlow level. There are significant differences between groups categorized by urban or rural area, teaching years and subject nature. Teachers mostly use generative AI for basic administrative tasks rather than seamlessly integrating it with subject teaching. Based on this, this study adapts the AITPACK theoretical model to generative AI contexts and builds a four dimensional composite AI teaching competence framework that includes AI general knowledge literacy, disciplinary teaching skills, AI educational ethical management skills and human machine collaborative research and innovation skills, and three levels of competence: entry level, proficient level and leading level. Hierarchical cultivation routes are suggested from three aspects: comprehensive planning by educational administrative departments, institutionalized schoolbased teaching research, and teachers' selforiented lifelong learning, along with supporting policies regarding institutional norms, resource allocation and performance appraisal. * * Empirical evidence indicates that teachers' teaching experience, disciplinary characteristics and the degree of digitalization of their schools have positive impacts on AI teaching competence development. Key barriers include scattered training resources, the absence of tiered courses for teachers with different proficiency levels, and the lack of ethics training in daily teaching practice. Theoretically, this study broadens the application scope of TPACK theory in generative AI environment and develops the theory system of teachers' digital competence cultivation in basic education. In practice, the built competency model and cultivation paths can be used as actionable plans for regional education administrators and primary-secondary schools to plan teachers' AI literacy training and support the deep integration of generative artificial intelligence into basic education teaching.
venue: Theory and Practice of Chinese Pedagogy

title_key: building a single classroom for app development peer video review as process evidence in a hybrid app development curriculum|cowling
title: Building a single classroom for app development: Peer video review as process evidence in a hybrid app development curriculum
abstract: Hybrid classes that split face-to-face and online students across separate rooms, timetables and (often) separate expectations risk becoming two separate classrooms within one class, rather than a single cohort. This paper reports the conceptual framing, literature context, intervention design and methodology of a study examining whether an intentionally designed, video-centred hybrid model can knit a dispersed cohort back into a single classroom, and whether the evidence it generates can say something more useful about learning than a finished app ever could. The study is set in an app development class at a university, where on-campus and online students learn iOS app development side by side. Building on an existing model for merging cohorts through the deliberate use of technology, the intervention layers a new practice onto shared lecture capture: students record and upload short videos of their app prototypes and code walkthroughs for structured peer review. The activity is designed both to strengthen interaction across the hybrid cohort and to foreground students’ thinking and development process, since every student contributes and reviews the same form of evidence regardless of study mode. Where a submitted app file is a product, a video walkthrough of how it was built and why is closer to a process, and in an era in which generative AI can produce a plausible product on demand, process is where the more trustworthy evidence of learning now sits. This concise paper sets out the problem, research questions, literature context, intervention design and methodology; findings will be reported once data collection is complete.

title_key: beyond the tool a systematic realist synthesis of cognitive agency in human genai interaction in higher education|li
title: Beyond the tool: a systematic realist synthesis of cognitive agency in human-GenAI interaction in higher education
abstract: Cognitive agency concerns learners’ effortful, self-directed control over reasoning with generative AI (GenAI). Building on an existing implementation-level classification of generative AI use, this review examines how cognitive work is allocated between learners and AI tools. Following PRISMA 2020, searches of Scopus and Web of Science (2021–2025) yielded 93 peer-reviewed studies, appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. A realist synthesis specified an a priori program theory crossing the type of work offloaded (extraneous versus germane; cognitive load theory) with processing of AI output (heuristic acceptance versus analytical scrutiny; dual-process theory), and audited the evidence on each axis under manifest coding (reported evidence only) and latent coding (adding design-based inference). Under manifest coding, 21 studies were located on both axes; all four configurations occurred, two in a single study each, and the nine Cognitive Extension studies reported peripheral uses with analytical scrutiny. Of the 93 studies, 49 reported no learner behavior toward AI output, 69 reported no learning measure independent of AI assistance, and four reported processing evidence together with such a measure. Group differences or part-sample outcomes were documented in 30 studies; one further study reported stage differences, but no learner-, task-, or assessment-level moderator showed an interpretable corpus-level association with substitution. This evidence profile identifies the process and AI-independent learning measures needed to distinguish cognitive extension from cognitive substitution. The review restates the Heterogeneous Pathways of Distributed Agency (HPDA) Model as seven testable propositions and specifies the process-tracing and AI-independent outcome designs needed to test them.
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education

title_key: awareness utilization and pedagogical integration of artificial intelligence ai tools in biology teaching among science teachers toward the development of a training program|limpo
title: Awareness, utilization, and pedagogical integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in biology teaching among science teachers: Toward the development of a training program
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to support instructional planning, the development of learning materials, assessment, and student engagement. However, the extent to which science teachers are aware of, utilize, and pedagogically integrate AI tools in Biology teaching remains an important concern. This study determined the awareness, utilization, and pedagogical integration of AI tools among junior high school science teachers in the Division of Tagbilaran City, Bohol, and examined the predictive contribution of these variables to teachers’ perceived teaching effectiveness and ability to promote student engagement. A quantitative approach using a descriptive-predictive research design was employed. The respondents were 32 junior high school science teachers teaching Biology in public secondary schools, selected through total enumeration. Data were gathered using an adapted structured questionnaire administered through Google Forms and analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and multiple linear regression. ChatGPT was the most recognized, currently used, and most useful AI tool. Teachers were aware of AI tools (M = 3.81), frequently utilized them in Biology instruction (M = 3.74), and occasionally integrated them pedagogically (M = 3.35). Their perceived teaching effectiveness and ability to promote student engagement were rated positively (M = 3.68). The regression model significantly predicted the outcome (R² = .603, F = 14.17, p < .001); however, only awareness was a statistically significant predictor (B = 0.450, p < .001). Utilization and pedagogical integration were not significant predictors. The findings informed a proposed professional development program to strengthen teachers’ AI literacy and support the effective, ethical, and curriculum-aligned integration of AI in Biology teaching.
venue: International Journal of Research Studies in Education

title_key: innovative pedagogy in elementary school mathematics education a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis|yuliandari
title: Innovative Pedagogy in Elementary School Mathematics Education: A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Innovative pedagogy has been at the heart of efforts to strengthen mathematics learning in early grades, but the field is still scattered among a wide range of technologies and rapidly evolving learning approaches. This study maps the scientific landscape of innovative pedagogy in elementary school mathematics education through systematic literature review combined with bibliometric analysis. By following the PRISMA 2020 protocol, a search of the Scopus database yielded 1,002 records, which were then filtered based on the criteria of subject area, focus, and document type so that a final corpus of 19 indexed and peer-reviewed articles published between 2021 and 2026 was obtained. The corpus was analyzed descriptively to see publication trends, geographic distribution, and source journals, and visualized through co-occurrence, co-authorship, and co-citation maps using VOSviewer. The findings show a sharp acceleration in recent times, with 58% of studies published in 2025–2026 and a noticeable shift towards artificial intelligence, large language model tutoring, augmented reality, and learning analytics. The thematic synthesis identifies four main strands: technology-assisted learning, teacher competence and readiness, inclusive and equitable practices, and assessment and feedback design. The bibliometric map shows a geographically fragmented field with very minimal cross-border collaboration and no representation from Indonesia. This study contributes an integrated and up-to-date picture of how innovation is reshaping primary school mathematics pedagogy and advocates contextually sensitive research to reach underrepresented backgrounds
venue: Proceeding of International Conference on Islamic Education

title_key: can genai numeracy tutors support self regulated learning|camacho
title: Can GenAI numeracy tutors support self-regulated learning?
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has been the focus of much attention in the higher education sector, both for its potential to support personalised and adaptive learning, but also due to the risk that students may outsource learning to it, leading to gaps in their professional or discipline competencies. This risk of cognitive offloading applies equally to learning how to learn, a skill set explored through studies of self-regulated learning (SRL). Two GenAI numeracy tutors were piloted at a regional Australian university as one component of a newly launched mathematics and statistics support centre, one focusing on medication calculations for Nursing students (NiNA), and the other on threshold numeracy skills for Education students (EdNA). Detailed analysis of students’ conversations with these agents using Zimmerman and Moylan’s 2009 SRL framework revealed extensive evidence of some elements of SRL such as strategic planning, task-specific strategies, and adaptive competence; trace evidence of other elements including self-efficacy and self-evaluation; and no evidence of the remaining elements. This study contributes an underrepresented qualitative perspective to the body of research into the crossover of GenAI and SRL and foreshadows avenues for further research and refinements in the design of GenAI numeracy tutors.

title_key: leveraging artificial intelligence as a virtual teaching assistant for technical writing|beetham
title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence As a Virtual Teaching Assistant for Technical Writing
abstract: Chat-style Artificial Intelligence (AI) assistants such as chat-GPT and Gemini, among others, have quickly risen to prominence in both educational and industrial spaces over the last year. Students’ use of these tools has become common place in all areas of education including studying and the carrying out of homework and other assessed. In light of this and its implications of academic integrity, most institutions have placed limitations on the use of AI tools in education. Indeed, while the reliance of these tools to circumvent the student’s learning is clearly damaging to long-term student success and understanding, these tools hold the potential to aid in the educational process when placed in proper context with reasonable constraints in place. In this work, we explore the incorporation of such tools as a ‘virtual teaching assistant’ for developing technical writing skills at the sophomore level in the context of a thermal-fluids sciences course. This work explores students’ attitudes toward the use of AI in developing laboratory reports and associated graphs, with MATLAB–a coding tool to which they’ve only had minimal exposure. We demonstrate that this approach holds promise for augmenting student learning, particularly for situations in which access to human teaching assistants are limited such as is the case for budget-limited programs.
venue: Volume 2: Fluid Measurement and Instrumentation; Energy & Sustainability; Multiphase Flows Applications; Fluids Applications; Microfluidics; Fluids Mechanics Fundamentals; Fluids Engineering Education; Memorial Session: Frank White Memorial

title_key: pelatihan pengembangan media pembelajaran interaktif berbasis ai untuk meningkatkan literasi ai bagi guru sdn 001 samarinda utara|tejawati
title: Pelatihan Pengembangan Media Pembelajaran Interaktif Berbasis AI Untuk Meningkatkan Literasi AI Bagi Guru SDN 001 Samarinda Utara
abstract: Elementary school teachers need artificial intelligence (AI) literacy as coding, and AI are introduced into the curriculum, yet SD Negeri 001 Samarinda Utara has limited facilities: there is no computer laboratory, not every teacher owns a laptop, Wi-Fi does not reach all rooms, and teachers' digital skills vary. This community service aimed to improve teachers' AI literacy by training them to develop AI-based learning media. The method was hands-on training with direct mentoring using ChatGPT and MagicSchool AI, both accessible via a browser or mobile phone and laptop. The training took place in September 2026 and 23 teachers attended. AI literacy was measured with identical pretest and posttest items, and participants' products were reviewed descriptively. The AI literacy score increased only slightly, not significantly, because most items were already answered correctly on the pretest. The clearest improvement was in understanding data security, whereas understanding of AI hallucination remained low. Most participants produced one student worksheet and one lesson presentation. Further training on evaluating AI outputs is still needed.
authors: ["Andi Tejawati", "Rajiansyah", "M. Wati", "Ummul Hairah", "H. Hatta", "M. Taruk", "Reza Wardhana", "Z. Arifin", "M. Firdaus", "Muhammad Ibnu Sa'ad", "Muhammad Haykal Makhmud", "Muhammad Farras Arhab Ince"]

title_key: scaffolding educator ai literacy the sage framework and the guard learning environment|rantanen
title: Scaffolding Educator AI Literacy: The SAGE Framework and the GUARD Learning Environment
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has moved from novelty to infrastructure in higher education within roughly two academic years, leaving educators caught between uncritical adoption and outright rejection. European policy frameworks increasingly call for AI-literate teaching, yet practical resources for translating high-level guidance into classroom practice remain scarce. This paper presents two outputs of the PATHFINDER project, an Erasmus+ Key Action 2 cooperation partnership involving the University of Liechtenstein, the University of Dubrovnik, LAB University of Applied Sciences, and formatio High School. The first output, Strategies for AI-Guided Education (SAGE), is an open instructional framework organised into four progressive modules: generative AI basics, prompt engineering, teaching with AI, and guiding students’ AI use. The second output, the GUARD learning environment (Generative Universal Assistant for Resourceful Development), operationalises the framework through a hands-on web application that combines Socratic scaffolding with a live large language model chat interface. GUARD scaffolds effective AI use through five practice-oriented learning labs, each structured around three iterations focused on intent formulation, critical evaluation, and ownership. The first lab, Plan a Class Activity, supports the design of a learning activity for a specific topic, audience, and objective. The second, Create a Learning Assessment, supports the development of formative or summative items aligned to a target cognitive level. The third, Design a Rubric, supports the construction of analytic or holistic rubrics with specific, observable descriptors. The fourth, Revise an Existing Curriculum, allows users to upload a syllabus and revise it for stronger alignment, coherence, and AI literacy integration. The fifth, Revise an Assignment for AI Use, allows users to upload and redesign assignments so that student AI use is addressed fairly while preserving meaningful assessment. We describe the conceptual grounding, design rationale, content architecture, and technical implementation of both resources, and discuss their relevance to current debates on educator AI literacy, scaffolded skill acquisition, and responsible AI integration. The paper contributes a concrete, transferable response to a challenge faced by educational institutions worldwide.

title_key: relationships among ai literacy critical evaluation of ai generated information and academic integrity among higher education students a cross sectional study with implications for assessment practice|rasbi
title: RELATIONSHIPS AMONG AI LITERACY, CRITICAL EVALUATION OF AI-GENERATED INFORMATION, AND ACADEMIC INTEGRITY AMONG HIGHER EDUCATION STUDENTS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY WITH IMPLICATIONS FOR ASSESSMENT PRACTICE
abstract: The integration of generative AI in higher education has sparked learning opportunities as well as concerns over students' ability to assess information generated by AI and ensure academic honesty. This study explored the relationships between the three measures, AI literacy, critical evaluation, and academic integrity, by analyzing the data from a quantitative, cross-sectional, openly available dataset of 972 students enrolled in higher education and 60 seven-point Likert items. The four domains of affective, behavioral, cognitive, and ethical dimensions of AI literacy were measured; critical evaluation was measured by the items of justification and verification; and academic integrity was reverse-scored as academic dishonesty. Descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha, Pearson and Spearman correlations, Welch's tests, partial correlations and sensitivity analysis were performed. The relationships were strong and positive between AI literacy and critical evaluation (r=.749, p<.001) and weak but positive between AI literacy and academic integrity (r=.171, p<.001). The relationship of ethical AI literacy towards academic dishonesty was the strongest negative one, and institutional difference was also found to be significant. The results suggest a stronger link between AI literacy with the critical evaluation than with integrity-related behaviour. The incorporation of verification, ethical considerations, and disclosure of the use of AI tools into the curriculum and policy of universities is therefore necessary.
authors: ["Tariq bin Juma bin Mohammad Al-Rasbi", "Rabi' bin Al-Mur Al-Dhahli", "Ahmed Mahmoud Radwan"]
venue: International journal for research in educational studies

title_key: smartphone based simulated photometer for teaching spectrophotometry using ai assisted tools|huang
title:
Smartphone-Based
Simulated Photometer for Teaching
Spectrophotometry Using AI-Assisted Tools
abstract: This study proposes an approach that uses generative artificial intelligence (AI) to develop a web application capable of interfacing with a smartphone camera and performing quantitative RGB-based chemical measurements. Using this method, students can readily convert their own smartphones into simple photometers for immediate use in the classroom. With teacher guidance, students employ AI agents to create HTML files that activate the smartphone camera and extract RGB values from captured images, converting light intensity measurements into absorbance data. Unlike conventional commercial software, which is generally immutable and operates as a closed system, this approach enables students to develop customized simulated photometers based on their unique design concepts by manipulating AI prompt inputs. By employing this approach, students are able to rapidly configure a simulated spectrophotometer utilizing solely their smartphones within the classroom environment, without the need for any additional external equipment, thereby enabling them to perform a range of simulated spectrophotometric experiments. By actively participating in the design of a simulated photometer and directly observing its operational process during hands-on manipulation, students can achieve a deeper understanding of the fundamental mechanisms and essential principles underlying spectrophotometry. Furthermore, this generative AI-based approach can also be applied to smartphone colorimetry, enabling users without any programming background to develop their own accessible analytical tools tailored to their practical demands, thereby greatly broadening the use of smartphone colorimetry in chemistry education and quantitative analysis.

title_key: teachers and students perspectives on the use of chatgpt in the research methods course a study at abu issa college of education university of zawia libya|algahwash
title: Teachers’ and Students’ Perspectives on the Use of ChatGPT in the Research Methods Course: A Study at Abu-Issa College of Education, University of Zawia, Libya
abstract: This study investigated teachers’ and students’ perspectives on the use of ChatGPT in the Research Methods course at Abu-Issa College of Education, University of Zawia. It aimed to explore students’ perceptions of ChatGPT, examine teachers’ views, identify its perceived benefits and challenges, and consider ways of promoting its responsible use in research-related learning. The study adopted a mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected through an online questionnaire administered to 30 seventh-semester students from the English Language Department, while qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with five teachers who had taught the Research Methods course. The questionnaire data were analysed using descriptive statistics, including frequencies, percentages, and mean scores, whereas the interview responses were examined thematically. The findings revealed that students generally held positive perceptions of ChatGPT and considered it a useful supplementary learning tool. Almost all students (96.7%) reported having used ChatGPT, while 90% indicated that they had used it for course-related purposes. Students particularly valued its ability to generate research ideas, develop research questions, explain difficult concepts, organise information, and improve academic writing. However, the findings also highlighted concerns regarding inaccurate information, unreliable references, excessive dependence on AI-generated responses, and potential negative effects on critical thinking and independent learning. Teachers similarly acknowledged its educational potential but emphasised the risks of copying generated content without sufficient understanding or critical evaluation. Furthermore, 73.3% of students reported receiving no formal guidance or training on responsible ChatGPT use. The study concludes that ChatGPT can support teaching and learning in Research Methods when accompanied by appropriate guidance, critical evaluation, academic integrity, and independent thinking. It recommends providing students with practical training and establishing clear institutional guidelines for its responsible integration into higher education.

title_key: humancentred engineering education for industry 5 0 with generative ai|jimenez
title: Human‐Centred Engineering Education for Industry 5.0 With Generative AI
abstract: The Industry 5.0 paradigm emphasises human capabilities, such as creative and analytical thinking, in complex environments that cooperate with highly autonomous systems powered by Artificial Intelligence. This underscores the need for advanced digital skills in education to prepare future workers capable of adapting to highly dynamic and demanding workplaces. This study utilises Challenge‐Based Learning (CBL) and Design Thinking (DT), to integrate Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) into the entire engineering learning process, considering both students and teacher perspectives, and to construct a creative and collaborative environment in which students collaborate with each other and with AI to solve complex real‐world problems. The experience was validated through a mixed‐methods approach including questionnaire surveys and semi‐structured interviews. The results indicate that students have a positive learning experience with the GenAI embedded into CBL, and there are generally no issues during the implementation process. Students also highlighted the importance of critically evaluating AI‐generated outputs and using these tools in a responsible manner. This study provides theoretical and practical guidance for integrating AI into high school learning, promoting active learning, efficient learning and human‐centred approaches aligned with the ethical and responsible use of these tools under the Industry 5.0 paradigm
